scr_cash_voiding_pending_payments.purpose: Voids one or more pending electronic payments inside a payment file that has not yet been confirmed — for example a vendor payment pulled because of a dispute or a bank-detail change that needs verification.
scr_cash_voiding_pending_payments.outcome: The specific payment is removed from the pending file and its invoice returns to open status, while the rest of the file proceeds.
scr_cash_voiding_pending_payments.rootCause: Problems with individual payments (a disputed invoice, a suspicious bank-detail change) are often found after the file is generated. Voiding one pending payment avoids holding up every other vendor in the file.
scr_cash_voiding_pending_payments.ifSkipped: Either the whole file is held and all vendors are paid late, or a questionable payment goes out and may be unrecoverable.
redFlags: Pending payments voided after the bank already processed the file

scr_cash_voiding_payments_from_the_check.purpose: Voids a check or electronic payment from the check register view by bank account — the standard route for lost checks, returned ACH payments, or payments issued in error.
scr_cash_voiding_payments_from_the_check.outcome: The payment is reversed in cash and A/P, and the invoice can be reissued or closed.
scr_cash_voiding_payments_from_the_check.rootCause: The check register is where accountants find payments by bank account and number when a vendor reports non-receipt or the bank returns an item. Voiding from there keeps the check sequence and bank rec aligned.
scr_cash_voiding_payments_from_the_check.ifSkipped: Lost or returned payments remain as outstanding items and the vendor stays unpaid.
redFlags: Voided checks without a bank stop-payment or positive pay void

scr_cash_voiding_a_confirmed_electronic_.purpose: Voids an electronic payment that the bank already confirmed — used when an ACH return (R01 insufficient funds, R03 no account, R04 invalid account) arrives days later or when funds were recovered from the vendor.
scr_cash_voiding_a_confirmed_electronic_.outcome: The returned funds are reflected in cash and the invoice is reopened for repayment.
scr_cash_voiding_a_confirmed_electronic_.rootCause: ACH returns arrive up to two banking days (and unauthorized returns up to 60 days) after settlement. The books show the vendor paid until the confirmed payment is voided.
scr_cash_voiding_a_confirmed_electronic_.ifSkipped: Vendors remain unpaid while the books show them paid, and returned cash sits as an unexplained deposit on the bank rec.
gaap: NACHA return reason codes and timeframes
redFlags: ACH returns on the bank statement not reflected in the check register

scr_cash_schedule_ach_file_generation_li.purpose: Lists scheduled ACH file generation jobs — which bank accounts, what time, how often — that automatically build payment files from approved payments.
scr_cash_schedule_ach_file_generation_li.outcome: Visibility of automated payment runs so treasury knows when files will be created and sent.
scr_cash_schedule_ach_file_generation_li.rootCause: Automated file schedules remove manual work but also remove a human checkpoint. Treasury needs to see and control every schedule that can move money.
scr_cash_schedule_ach_file_generation_li.ifSkipped: Unknown or forgotten schedules send payments at unexpected times or from the wrong account.
gaap: COSO 2013 — IT general controls over automated jobs
redFlags: Schedules owned by terminated users
Schedules on accounts that no longer exist

scr_cash_scheduling_an_ach_payment_file.purpose: Creates a schedule for automatic ACH file generation — selecting bank accounts, frequency and time before the bank's cut-off.
scr_cash_scheduling_an_ach_payment_file.outcome: Approved vendor payments are packaged into files automatically and reliably before the cut-off.
scr_cash_scheduling_an_ach_payment_file.rootCause: Manual file generation depends on someone remembering before cut-off, which fails across time zones. A schedule makes payment timing predictable for vendors.
scr_cash_scheduling_an_ach_payment_file.ifSkipped: Payments miss cut-offs and vendors are paid a day or more late.
redFlags: Schedule time set after the bank's same-day ACH cut-off

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_scheduled_.purpose: Reviews or changes a scheduled ACH file generation job — which originating bank accounts it covers, the run time relative to the bank's ACH cut-off, and its frequency.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_scheduled_.outcome: Automated payment runs stay aligned with current bank cut-offs and the accounts that actually pay vendors.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_scheduled_.rootCause: Banks move cut-off times and properties change banks after refinancing. A schedule left on the old settings either misses the cut-off (late payments) or tries to pay from an account that no longer exists.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_scheduled_.ifSkipped: Scheduled runs keep firing against outdated accounts or times, and vendors are paid late without anyone noticing.
gaap: COSO 2013 — change management over automated jobs
redFlags: Schedule edits made without a second approver

scr_cash_viewing_execution_logs_for_a_sc.purpose: Shows the run history of a scheduled ACH job — when it ran, how many payments were included, and whether it succeeded or failed.
scr_cash_viewing_execution_logs_for_a_sc.outcome: Treasury can confirm each scheduled run produced the expected file and investigate failures quickly.
scr_cash_viewing_execution_logs_for_a_sc.rootCause: Automated jobs fail silently (expired credentials, empty batches). Logs are the only evidence that payments actually went out as scheduled.
scr_cash_viewing_execution_logs_for_a_sc.ifSkipped: Failed runs go unnoticed and vendors are not paid.
redFlags: Consecutive failed runs without follow-up

scr_cash_turning_a_payment_file_schedule.purpose: Pauses or resumes a scheduled ACH file job — for example during a bank migration, a suspected fraud investigation or a holiday.
scr_cash_turning_a_payment_file_schedule.outcome: Automated payments can be stopped immediately without deleting the schedule setup.
scr_cash_turning_a_payment_file_schedule.rootCause: When fraud is suspected or bank details are changing, automated payment flows must be halted quickly and restarted cleanly afterward.
scr_cash_turning_a_payment_file_schedule.ifSkipped: Payments continue during an investigation or bank migration, possibly to compromised accounts.
redFlags: Schedules left off after the reason was resolved, delaying vendor payments

scr_cash_deleting_a_scheduled_ach_paymen.purpose: Deletes a scheduled ACH file job that is no longer needed, such as after a bank account is closed or a property is sold.
scr_cash_deleting_a_scheduled_ach_paymen.outcome: Obsolete schedules cannot trigger unexpected payment files.
scr_cash_deleting_a_scheduled_ach_paymen.rootCause: Every active schedule is a standing instruction to move money. Removing those that no longer apply reduces the risk of unexpected payments.
scr_cash_deleting_a_scheduled_ach_paymen.ifSkipped: Old schedules may run against reused or re-mapped accounts.
redFlags: Schedules remaining for sold properties

scr_cash_credit_card_transactions_list.purpose: Lists transactions recorded against company credit card accounts — purchases by site staff, card payments to vendors, and payments of the card balance.
scr_cash_credit_card_transactions_list.outcome: A register of card activity that can be matched to the issuer's monthly statement and coded to properties.
scr_cash_credit_card_transactions_list.rootCause: Card purchases bypass POs and invoice approval. Recording them individually with coding is how they get reviewed and charged to the right property.
scr_cash_credit_card_transactions_list.ifSkipped: Card charges are paid in one lump from the statement without property coding or review.
redFlags: Card transactions without receipts
Split transactions to avoid card limits

scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.purpose: Records a card purchase — card account, date, merchant, amount, property and GL coding — so the expense and card liability are recognized when incurred.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.outcome: Card spending is recorded in the right property and period with the card liability.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.rootCause: Card statements arrive after month-end. Recording transactions as they occur puts the expense in the right month and allows review before payment.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.ifSkipped: Card expenses are recorded a month late and without review.
redFlags: Personal merchants (restaurants, retail) coded to operating expenses

scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_transacti.purpose: Edits a card transaction entered directly in Cash Management (not one generated from A/P) — correcting coding, date or amount.
scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_transacti.outcome: Card transaction coding is corrected before statement reconciliation.
scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_transacti.rootCause: Direct entries can be corrected in place; transactions tied to A/P invoice payments must be corrected in A/P to keep the invoice trail intact.
scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_transacti.ifSkipped: Coding errors persist or corrections break the link to A/P invoices.
redFlags: Edits after the statement was reconciled

scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_transac.purpose: Reverses a card transaction entered in error or refunded by the merchant; transactions tied to A/P invoice payments are reversed through the payment instead.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_transac.outcome: The card liability and expense are corrected with an audit trail.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_transac.rootCause: Merchant refunds and duplicate entries must reduce both the expense and the card liability so the card reconciles to the statement.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_transac.ifSkipped: The card account shows a higher balance than the issuer and expenses are overstated.
redFlags: Refunds on the statement not reflected

scr_cash_credit_card_transaction_informa.purpose: The record page for a card transaction showing card account, merchant, date, amount, distribution and attachments such as the receipt.
scr_cash_credit_card_transaction_informa.outcome: Full detail and receipt for each card charge, supporting review and audit.
scr_cash_credit_card_transaction_informa.rootCause: Auditors and reviewers test card charges for business purpose; the receipt and coding must sit together.
scr_cash_credit_card_transaction_informa.ifSkipped: Card charges lack evidence of business purpose.
gaap: IRS substantiation rules for business expenses (IRC §274(d))
redFlags: Missing receipts on charges over the policy threshold

scr_cash_charge_payoffs_list.purpose: Lists card charges that need to be paid off — the charges that make up the card statement balance — used to record the payment to the card issuer against specific charges.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_list.outcome: Card balances are paid down against identified charges, keeping the card liability detail clean.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_list.rootCause: Paying the issuer a lump sum without tying it to charges leaves the liability detail unreconcilable. Charge payoffs match payments to what was charged.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_list.ifSkipped: The card liability account accumulates unmatched charges and payments.
redFlags: Old unpaid charges remaining on the list

scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff.purpose: Records a payment to the credit card issuer and selects the specific card charges it pays off, so the card liability detail shows exactly which purchases have been settled.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff.outcome: The card liability is reduced charge by charge, and any charges left unpaid stand out before late fees and interest accrue.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff.rootCause: Paying the issuer a lump sum without tying it to charges leaves the card liability impossible to reconcile to the statement, and unpaid charges hide inside the balance until interest appears.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff.ifSkipped: Card payments cannot be matched to statements, late fees accrue on overlooked balances, and the card liability drifts from the issuer's figure.
redFlags: Payoff amount different from the statement's amount due

scr_cash_reversing_a_charge_payoff.purpose: Reverses a charge payoff (it cannot be edited because the system generates its entries), for example when the payment to the issuer was returned or recorded for the wrong charges.
scr_cash_reversing_a_charge_payoff.outcome: The card liability and cash are restored and the payoff can be re-entered correctly.
scr_cash_reversing_a_charge_payoff.rootCause: System-generated postings are locked to protect the audit trail; reversal is the controlled correction.
scr_cash_reversing_a_charge_payoff.ifSkipped: Returned card payments remain recorded as paid.
redFlags: Reversals without re-entry

scr_cash_charge_payoffs_information.purpose: Explains the charge payoff record — payment date, amount, issuer and the charges covered.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_information.outcome: Clear understanding of how card payments link to charges.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_information.rootCause: Users need to know the payoff structure to reconcile the card liability and answer cardholder or issuer questions.
scr_cash_charge_payoffs_information.ifSkipped: Card reconciliations are performed without understanding which payments covered which charges.
redFlags: Payoffs with no linked charges

scr_cash_positive_pay_file_list.purpose: Lists positive pay files generated for each bank account — the issued-check lists sent to banks — and allows manual generation when the automatic file did not run.
scr_cash_positive_pay_file_list.outcome: Treasury can confirm every check run and manual check was reported to the bank before the checks were presented.
scr_cash_positive_pay_file_list.rootCause: Positive pay only protects checks that are on the file. The list is where treasury confirms files went out for every issuing account every day checks were written.
scr_cash_positive_pay_file_list.ifSkipped: Checks are issued without positive pay coverage, exposing the account to counterfeit and altered checks.
gaap: UCC 3-406 / 4-406 — loss allocation for check fraud
redFlags: Check run dates with no corresponding positive pay file

scr_cash_deleting_a_positive_pay_file.purpose: Deletes a positive pay file from the list — typically one generated with errors — so it can be regenerated correctly.
scr_cash_deleting_a_positive_pay_file.outcome: The bank receives an accurate issued-check list rather than a wrong one.
scr_cash_deleting_a_positive_pay_file.rootCause: A wrong positive pay file causes legitimate checks to be rejected or fraudulent ones to be accepted; replacing it requires removing the wrong version first.
scr_cash_deleting_a_positive_pay_file.ifSkipped: Incorrect files stay on record and may be resent.
redFlags: Files deleted after transmission without notifying the bank

scr_cash_generate_positive_pay_file_page.purpose: The page to manually generate a positive pay file for selected bank accounts and date ranges.
scr_cash_generate_positive_pay_file_page.outcome: An on-demand issued-check file covering checks not included in automatic files.
scr_cash_generate_positive_pay_file_page.rootCause: Manual checks and off-schedule runs are the checks most likely to be missing from automatic positive pay files.
scr_cash_generate_positive_pay_file_page.ifSkipped: Manual checks are not protected and legitimate ones may be rejected.
redFlags: Date ranges that skip days

scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_list.purpose: Lists bank interest earned and bank charges (service fees, analysis fees, wire fees) recorded from bank statements for each account.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_list.outcome: A register of bank-originated income and fees recorded in the correct period and property.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_list.rootCause: Banks post interest and fees that never pass through A/P or A/R. Unless recorded, they remain reconciling items and are missing from the P&L.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_list.ifSkipped: Bank fees and interest are missing from the income statement and recs show recurring unexplained items.
gaap: State rules on interest owed to residents on security deposits
redFlags: Interest on security deposit trust accounts recorded as property income where state law requires it be credited to residents

scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_or_charges.purpose: Records bank interest or charges from the statement — account, date, amount and GL account — with defaults available for recurring items.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_or_charges.outcome: Bank-originated activity is booked so the reconciliation clears.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_or_charges.rootCause: Defaults for recurring charges make monthly entry quick and consistent across accounts.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_or_charges.ifSkipped: Recurring bank fees remain unrecorded reconciling items.
redFlags: Fees coded to administrative expense instead of bank charges

scr_cash_editing_a_bank_interest_or_char.purpose: Edits an unposted or editable bank interest or charge entry to fix amount, date or GL coding.
scr_cash_editing_a_bank_interest_or_char.outcome: Bank fee entries match the statement exactly.
scr_cash_editing_a_bank_interest_or_char.rootCause: Small keying errors in bank fees prevent the reconciliation from balancing to the penny.
scr_cash_editing_a_bank_interest_or_char.ifSkipped: Recs do not balance and preparers force them with plugs.
redFlags: Edits after the reconciliation was finalized

scr_cash_reversing_a_bank_interest_or_ch.purpose: Reverses a posted bank interest or charge — for example a fee the bank later refunded or one recorded twice.
scr_cash_reversing_a_bank_interest_or_ch.outcome: Duplicate or refunded fees are removed with an audit trail.
scr_cash_reversing_a_bank_interest_or_ch.rootCause: Banks refund disputed fees; recording the refund as a reversal keeps the fee history clear.
scr_cash_reversing_a_bank_interest_or_ch.ifSkipped: Fees are overstated and the rec shows an unexplained credit.
redFlags: Reversals without bank evidence

scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_infor.purpose: The record page for a bank interest or charge with account, date, amount and GL distribution.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_infor.outcome: Complete detail for each bank-originated entry.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_infor.rootCause: Reviewers need to trace each fee or interest entry to the statement line it came from.
scr_cash_bank_interest_and_charges_infor.ifSkipped: Fee entries cannot be traced to statements.
redFlags: Entries without statement references

scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.purpose: Lists fees charged on company credit cards — annual fees, late fees, interest, foreign transaction fees — recorded from card statements.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.outcome: Card fees are recorded as expenses so card accounts reconcile.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.rootCause: Card fees appear only on statements; like bank fees, they must be booked to reconcile the card liability.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.ifSkipped: Card liability does not tie to the statement.
redFlags: Recurring late fees indicating payment process failures

scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_charge_or_.purpose: Records a fee or interest charge that appears on a company credit card statement — annual fee, late fee, foreign transaction fee or finance charge — against the card account.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_charge_or_.outcome: The card liability matches the issuer statement and the fee is expensed in the right period.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_charge_or_.rootCause: Issuer fees and interest are only visible on the statement; nothing in A/P generates them. Until recorded, the card reconciliation is off by exactly those amounts, and recurring late fees point to a broken payment routine.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_charge_or_.ifSkipped: Card reconciliations fail by the unrecorded fees, and repeated late fees go unnoticed.
reports: Credit card charges and fees list
redFlags: Finance charges recorded as bank charges
Late fees recurring on the same card

scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_charge_or.purpose: Edits a recorded card fee to correct amount, date or coding before reconciliation.
scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_charge_or.outcome: Card fees match the statement exactly.
scr_cash_editing_a_credit_card_charge_or.rootCause: Small keying errors keep the card reconciliation from balancing and lead to plugs.
redFlags: Edits after reconciliation finalized

scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_charge_.purpose: Reverses a recorded card fee — for example when the issuer waives a late fee after a dispute, or when a fee was entered twice.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_charge_.outcome: Waived or duplicate fees are removed from expense and the card liability with a clear trail.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_charge_.rootCause: Issuers often refund fees on request; the refund appears as a credit on the next statement. Reversing the original fee keeps expense and the card liability aligned with the issuer.
scr_cash_reversing_a_credit_card_charge_.ifSkipped: Card liability and bank-charge expense stay overstated and the next reconciliation shows an unexplained credit.
redFlags: Reversals not supported by a statement credit

scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.purpose: The record page for a card fee or interest charge, showing the card account, statement date, amount and GL distribution, so each fee can be traced to the issuer statement line.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.outcome: Traceable, reviewable detail for every card fee posted.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.rootCause: Reviewers test card fees for legitimacy and for signs of process failures (late fees, over-limit fees). Each fee must be traceable to the statement to support that review.
scr_cash_credit_card_charges_and_other_f.ifSkipped: Card fee entries cannot be verified and patterns like recurring late fees are hard to spot.
reports: Credit card charges and fees list
redFlags: Fees without a statement reference

scr_cash_reconciliation_box.purpose: Opening dialog of the new bank reconciliation tool where the accountant selects the bank account and statement date, sets up a first-time reconciliation, adds initial open items and imports the bank file.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box.outcome: The reconciliation session starts with the right account, the right statement period and the bank's transactions loaded.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box.rootCause: Starting with the wrong account or statement date is the root of many unbalanced recs. The box forces those choices up front and loads the bank data the matching depends on.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box.ifSkipped: Recs are started against the wrong period or without bank data, forcing manual matching.
redFlags: Statement ending balance keyed rather than taken from the bank file

scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.purpose: Procedure for the first reconciliation of an account in the new tool — entering the starting statement balance and loading outstanding checks and deposits in transit from the prior system or prior reconciliation.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.outcome: A correct starting point so every later reconciliation rolls forward cleanly.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.rootCause: When a property is onboarded or migrated from Yardi or another system, the outstanding items from the last prior-system reconciliation must be loaded. A wrong opening position breaks every future month.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.ifSkipped: The first rec is forced with a plug and the error carries forward indefinitely.
redFlags: First reconciliation balanced with an unexplained adjustment

scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.purpose: Selects the checking or savings account and statement date to reconcile in the new tool, and triggers first-time setup if the account has never been reconciled.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.outcome: The correct account and period are chosen for the reconciliation.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.rootCause: Portfolios hold many similarly named accounts (operating and trust accounts at the same bank). Selecting the wrong one produces a meaningless reconciliation.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.ifSkipped: Reconciliations are performed on the wrong account.
redFlags: Account last-four digits not matching the statement

scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items.purpose: Enters the outstanding checks and deposits in transit that existed before the first reconciliation in the new tool.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items.outcome: Prior outstanding items are carried into the new reconciliation so they can clear when they hit the bank.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items.rootCause: Items issued before the migration will clear afterwards. Without being loaded, they appear as unexplained bank activity.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items.ifSkipped: Pre-migration items show up as unmatched bank transactions for months.
redFlags: Initial open items total not equal to the prior system's outstanding list

scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items.purpose: Imports the initial outstanding items list from a file — usually the last outstanding check list from the prior system.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items.outcome: Large lists of outstanding items are loaded accurately in one step.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items.rootCause: Acquired properties can carry hundreds of outstanding items; keying them invites errors.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items.ifSkipped: Manually keyed items contain errors that break the first reconciliation.
redFlags: Import totals not reconciled to the source list

scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.purpose: Exports the initial open items loaded into the new reconciliation tool so they can be checked against the prior system's final outstanding check and deposit list.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.outcome: Independent verification that the migrated outstanding items are complete and accurate.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.rootCause: Opening items are loaded once, during conversion, often under deadline. An exported list lets a second person compare them to the prior system before they become the base for every future reconciliation.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.ifSkipped: Conversion errors in opening items go unverified and later surface as unexplained reconciling items that nobody can trace.
redFlags: No evidence that opening items were verified

scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file.purpose: Imports the bank's transaction file (CSV or BAI) into the new reconciliation so bank lines can be matched to book transactions automatically.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file.outcome: Bank activity is loaded exactly as the bank recorded it, enabling auto-matching.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file.rootCause: Keying bank transactions by hand introduces errors and is slow. Importing the bank's own data makes the bank side of the reconciliation objective.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file.ifSkipped: Manual keying errors and slow reconciliations.
redFlags: Bank file date range not matching the statement period

scr_cash_bank_reconciliation_legacy.purpose: The legacy bank reconciliation tool still used for some accounts, where the accountant selects the account, enters statement information and matches book transactions to the bank.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliation_legacy.outcome: Accounts not yet moved to the new tool still get a complete monthly reconciliation.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliation_legacy.rootCause: Companies migrate to the new tool gradually; the legacy tool remains for accounts with open history there. Both must produce equally reliable reconciliations.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliation_legacy.ifSkipped: Accounts left on the legacy tool are skipped during migration and go unreconciled.
redFlags: Accounts reconciled in both tools for the same period

scr_cash_reconciliation_box_2.purpose: Opening dialog of the legacy reconciliation tool where the accountant selects the bank account, enters the statement date and ending balance, sets up a first-time rec and imports the bank file.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box_2.outcome: A legacy reconciliation session started with the correct account, period and bank data.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box_2.rootCause: In the legacy tool, the choice of account and statement ending balance is where most unbalanced recs begin — keying the ending balance from the wrong page of a statement is a classic error.
scr_cash_reconciliation_box_2.ifSkipped: Legacy recs are started on wrong periods or balances and preparers force them with plugs.
redFlags: Ending balance not matching the bank statement

scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.purpose: Legacy-tool procedure for the first reconciliation of an account, setting the opening balance and loading pre-existing outstanding items.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.outcome: A correct opening position for legacy reconciliations.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.rootCause: First reconciliations in the legacy tool carry the same conversion risk: a wrong opening position breaks all later months.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account_for_.ifSkipped: Plugs at the first reconciliation that persist.
redFlags: Opening differences not documented

scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.purpose: Selects the checking or savings account to reconcile in the legacy tool, launching first-time setup if the account has never been reconciled there.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.outcome: The correct account is reconciled for the period in the legacy tool.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.rootCause: Properties often have an operating account and a security deposit trust account at the same bank with near-identical names. Selecting by account number rather than name prevents reconciling the wrong one.
scr_cash_selecting_an_account_to_reconci.ifSkipped: The wrong account is reconciled and the real one goes unreconciled for the month.
redFlags: Account last-four digits not matching the statement

scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items_2.purpose: Legacy-tool entry of outstanding items that existed before the first reconciliation in RealPage Accounting.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items_2.outcome: Pre-existing outstanding checks and deposits are carried into the legacy reconciliation.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items_2.rootCause: Without opening items, pre-conversion checks clearing later look like unexplained withdrawals.
scr_cash_adding_initial_open_items_2.ifSkipped: Unmatched bank items for pre-conversion activity.
redFlags: Opening items not tied to the prior reconciliation

scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items_2.purpose: Imports the list of pre-existing outstanding checks and deposits in transit into the legacy reconciliation tool from a file, typically the last outstanding list from the prior system.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items_2.outcome: Opening outstanding items are loaded accurately and completely in one step.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items_2.rootCause: Acquired or migrated properties can carry hundreds of outstanding checks. Keying them is slow and error-prone, and any error becomes a permanent reconciling difference.
scr_cash_importing_initial_open_items_2.ifSkipped: Keyed errors in opening items create reconciling differences that persist for months.
redFlags: Import totals not reconciled to the source list

scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.purpose: Exports initial open items from the legacy tool, in CSV for moving to the new tool or for verification.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.outcome: Opening items can be carried to the new tool or reviewed.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.rootCause: Migrating from the legacy to the new reconciliation tool requires carrying outstanding items across accurately.
scr_cash_exporting_the_initial_open_item.ifSkipped: Outstanding items lost in migration between tools.
redFlags: Export not reconciled after import into the new tool

scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file_2.purpose: Imports a CSV or BAI bank file into the legacy reconciliation to load the bank's transactions for matching.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file_2.outcome: Bank activity is loaded exactly as the bank recorded it for legacy matching.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file_2.rootCause: Manually keying bank activity into the legacy tool is slow and introduces errors that make the reconciliation fail. Importing the bank's own data keeps the bank side objective.
scr_cash_importing_a_bank_file_2.ifSkipped: Keying errors lead to unbalanced recs and plugs.
redFlags: The same bank file imported twice
